title: TMJ Pain and Your Bite: When to See a Dentist
seoTitle: TMJ Pain and Your Bite: When to See a Dentist | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: Clicking jaw, morning headaches, difficulty chewing — these are signs of TMJ disorder. Learn how bite alignment contributes to TMJ pain and when to seek dental care in Markham.
excerpt: The temporomandibular joint is one of the most complex joints in the body, and when it is under chronic strain — often from a misaligned bite or bruxism — the symptoms can include jaw pain, clicking, headaches and neck tension. This article explains the connection and what treatment can help.
intro: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) connects your lower jaw to your skull on each side of your face. It is active in virtually every function of the oral cavity: chewing, speaking, yawning, swallowing. When this joint is under chronic strain — whether from a bite that is not well-aligned, from grinding and clenching, or from injury — the resulting symptoms can range from mild jaw discomfort to debilitating pain that extends into the face, head and neck.

This article explains what causes TMJ disorder, how bite alignment relates to joint health, what symptoms warrant a dental evaluation, and what treatment options are available at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) in Markham.

sections.heading: Understanding the Temporomandibular Joint

blocks.text: The TMJ is a hinge-and-sliding joint — it both rotates (when you open slightly) and translates forward (when you open wide). A small cartilage disc sits between the ball of the lower jaw and the socket in the skull, cushioning the joint during all these movements. Ligaments stabilise the joint; a group of muscles — the masseter, temporalis, pterygoids and others — control its movement and bear the forces of chewing, which can reach over 100 pounds per square inch on the back teeth.

Because the TMJ operates continuously throughout every waking hour, and often throughout the night for patients who clench or grind, it is susceptible to cumulative strain. Small imbalances — a bite that causes the jaw to deviate slightly to one side to close, for example — translate into thousands of slightly asymmetric joint movements per day, gradually irritating the joint, the disc and the surrounding soft tissue.

sections.heading: How Bite Misalignment Contributes to TMJ Problems

blocks.text: When the upper and lower teeth do not occlude (meet) evenly, the jaw must shift into an unnatural position to achieve maximum tooth contact for chewing. This shift is unconscious — the neuromuscular system adapts automatically to bring as many teeth into contact as possible. The problem is that achieving maximum tooth contact by shifting the jaw also means the TMJ is not in its most anatomically ideal position, creating chronic strain on the joint and the muscles that hold the jaw in that adapted position.

Common bite problems that stress the TMJ include: significant overbite (deep bite), underbite, crossbite, and missing teeth that have allowed adjacent teeth to drift and change the bite. Orthodontic correction — through [Invisalign](/blog/invisalign-markham-cost-timeline) or traditional braces — addresses the root cause in these cases and often produces meaningful improvement in TMJ symptoms once the bite is corrected.

sections.heading: Recognising TMJ Disorder Symptoms

blocks.text: TMJ disorder (also called temporomandibular disorder or TMD) produces a range of symptoms that patients do not always associate with their jaw. The classic presentation includes jaw pain or tenderness, especially on waking, and clicking or popping sounds when opening or closing the mouth. The sounds alone, without pain, are common and not always clinically significant — it is the combination of sound with pain, locking, or limited opening that warrants evaluation.

items: Jaw pain or tenderness on one or both sides, especially on waking.
Clicking, popping or grating sounds in the jaw joint when opening or closing.
Limited jaw opening — inability to open as wide as normal without pain.
Jaw locking — momentary inability to fully open or close the jaw.
Headaches at the temples, behind the eyes or at the base of the skull.
Ear pain, fullness or ringing (tinnitus) without a clear ear cause.
Neck and shoulder tension that worsens with jaw clenching.

sections.heading: The Role of Bruxism in TMJ Strain

blocks.text: Bruxism — the habitual grinding and clenching of teeth — is one of the most significant drivers of TMJ disorder. During sleep, clenching forces can reach two to three times those of normal chewing, applied continuously for hours. The muscles involved become chronically overworked, developing the same kind of tension and soreness that skeletal muscles develop after prolonged exercise. Morning jaw soreness and temporal headaches are classic signatures of nocturnal bruxism.

A custom night guard is the most effective way to protect the joint and teeth from bruxism forces during sleep. It reduces the muscle activity of clenching and prevents the enamel-on-enamel contact that damages teeth over time. If bruxism is also driven by a bite misalignment, addressing the bite issue with orthodontics — including [Invisalign](/dental-services) — may reduce the grinding trigger itself. For more on the night guard side of this discussion, see our [night guards vs. Invisalign article](/blog/night-guards-vs-invisalign).

sections.heading: When to See a Dentist for Jaw Pain

blocks.text: Not every jaw click requires treatment — isolated, painless clicking is common and often benign. However, you should seek a dental evaluation when: jaw pain persists beyond a few days, clicking is accompanied by pain or limited opening, you wake regularly with jaw or temple soreness, or your jaw locks or catches during normal function. Early evaluation allows for conservative treatment before the condition progresses.

If your dentist suspects TMJ disorder they will examine the joint directly — palpating the muscles and joint for tenderness, measuring jaw opening, listening for joint sounds and assessing your bite. X-rays show the bony structures; occasionally an MRI is needed to visualise the cartilage disc. Most TMJ cases are managed by dentists without specialist referral, though complex cases involving significant disc displacement may benefit from evaluation by an oral and maxillofacial specialist.

sections.heading: Treatment Options for TMJ Disorder

blocks.text: The great majority of TMJ disorder cases resolve or improve significantly with conservative treatment. **Night guards** reduce clenching forces and allow the muscles and joint to rest during sleep. **Physiotherapy** targeting the jaw muscles — including stretching exercises, heat therapy and manual release techniques — is highly effective for muscle-dominant TMD. **Anti-inflammatory medication** (ibuprofen) during acute flares reduces pain and inflammation. **Stress management** matters enormously: anxiety and stress are major drivers of clenching, and addressing the psychological component produces meaningful clinical improvement.

When bite misalignment is a clear contributing factor, orthodontic treatment is appropriate. When missing teeth have caused bite collapse, dental restoration (including implants, crowns or dentures) addresses the underlying structural problem. Surgical intervention is rarely necessary and is reserved for disc displacement that does not respond to conservative treatment.

sections.heading: Getting Evaluated in Markham

blocks.text: Dr. Neda Kadivar has significant experience in diagnosing and managing TMJ disorder in the context of overall bite health. At Smile Dental Arts Centre, a TMJ evaluation includes a comprehensive bite analysis, muscle palpation, a review of your symptom history and — where orthodontic issues are suspected — a ClinCheck simulation showing what bite correction would involve. Treatment plans are conservative and sequenced: the simplest effective intervention first, with escalation only if needed.

[Book an appointment](/appointments) in Markham if you are experiencing any of the symptoms described above. TMJ problems that are addressed early respond much better to conservative treatment than those that have been present for years. We are available Monday through Friday with extended evening hours and every other Saturday.

title: How Much Does Invisalign Really Cost After Insurance?
seoTitle: Invisalign Cost After Insurance in Ontario | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: Wondering what Invisalign costs out-of-pocket after insurance in Ontario? Learn what plans typically cover, how to maximise your benefit and what financing options are available.
excerpt: Most Ontario dental plans include an orthodontic benefit that significantly reduces Invisalign costs — but understanding what you will actually pay out-of-pocket requires knowing exactly how your plan works. This guide breaks it down clearly.
intro: The headline price for Invisalign in Markham is typically $3,000 to $7,500 — but for most patients with employer-sponsored dental benefits, the actual out-of-pocket cost is considerably lower. Ontario group dental plans almost universally include an orthodontic benefit, and that benefit applies to Invisalign just as it applies to traditional braces, making the choice between the two a matter of clinical fit rather than insurance penalty.

This guide explains exactly how orthodontic insurance benefits work in Ontario, what a typical benefit covers and what it leaves uncovered, how to read your benefit booklet, and what financing options are available at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) for the remaining balance after insurance.

sections.heading: How Orthodontic Insurance Benefits Work

blocks.text: Orthodontic benefits in Ontario group plans typically operate differently from regular dental benefits. Rather than covering a percentage of each appointment, orthodontic benefits are usually paid as a percentage of the total treatment fee — commonly 50 percent — up to a lifetime maximum per covered person. The lifetime maximum is the most important number to know: it applies once per covered person for their lifetime under the plan, not per year.

For example, a plan with 50 percent coverage and a $2,500 lifetime orthodontic maximum would pay $2,500 toward a $5,000 Invisalign case — leaving $2,500 out of pocket. Orthodontic benefits are paid in installments over the course of active treatment rather than in a lump sum: the insurer typically pays a portion at the start of treatment and the remainder in equal monthly or quarterly installments as treatment progresses.

sections.heading: Does Insurance Cover Invisalign Specifically?

blocks.text: Yes — virtually all Ontario dental plans that include orthodontic benefits cover Invisalign on equal terms with traditional braces. The [Canadian Dental Association](https://www.cda-adc.ca/) codes used for comprehensive orthodontic treatment do not specify the appliance type, and insurers do not differentiate between Invisalign and braces for reimbursement purposes. If your plan covers braces, it covers Invisalign for the same amount.

The only scenario where Invisalign-specific exclusions appear is in very old legacy benefit booklets written before Invisalign became mainstream — and even these are increasingly rare. If you have any doubt, call your insurer directly and ask: does the orthodontic benefit apply equally to clear aligner treatment such as Invisalign? Get the answer in writing or reference number format.

sections.heading: What Plans Typically Do Not Cover

blocks.text: While the orthodontic benefit covers the main Invisalign treatment fee, several related costs may fall outside the benefit: the initial consultation fee (if charged separately), records fees for x-rays and digital scans, replacement aligners beyond those included in the manufacturer's replacement policy, and retainers at the end of treatment. Some plans include retainers within the orthodontic benefit; others treat them as a prosthetic and cover them under a different section; still others exclude them.

Understanding these potential gaps before treatment begins allows you to budget accurately. At our Markham clinic, the treatment coordinator prepares a written estimate showing the all-inclusive treatment fee, the expected insurance contribution based on your specific benefit, and your estimated out-of-pocket balance — before you sign any treatment agreement.

items: Lifetime orthodontic maximum — the single most important number; typically $1,500–$3,500.
Percentage covered — usually 50% of eligible fees up to the lifetime maximum.
Waiting periods — some plans have 12–24 month waits for new enrollees.
Age limits — some plans cover orthodontics only for dependents under age 18 or 21.
Retainers — check whether your plan covers retainers within the orthodontic benefit or separately.

sections.heading: Coordinating Two Plans (Dual Coverage)

blocks.text: Patients who have coverage under two plans — for example, their own employer plan and their spouse's employer plan — can coordinate benefits to significantly reduce out-of-pocket costs. In dual coverage, the primary plan pays first up to its lifetime maximum; the secondary plan then pays a portion of the remaining balance. Combined, dual coverage can sometimes cover 80–100 percent of Invisalign costs for patients whose plans have generous lifetime orthodontic maximums.

Our billing team is experienced in coordinating dual orthodontic coverage and will manage the submission to both insurers on your behalf. Bring benefit cards for both plans to your consultation so we can run a benefit check on both before developing your financial plan.

sections.heading: The Canadian Dental Care Plan and Orthodontics

blocks.text: The federal [Canadian Dental Care Plan](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/dental/dental-care-plan.html) is available to households with adjusted net family income below $90,000 who do not have access to private dental insurance. The CDCP covers some orthodontic services for children and youth, though the scope and fee schedule for orthodontics under this program continues to evolve. If your household qualifies for the CDCP, bring your benefit card to your consultation and we will run a benefit check to determine what is covered.

Adult orthodontics under the CDCP is more limited; coverage in this area is primarily focused on preventing functional problems rather than elective aesthetic treatment. However, cases where misalignment causes documented functional difficulty may qualify for some coverage even for adult patients. Our administrative team stays current on CDCP updates and will advise you on the latest eligibility criteria.

sections.heading: Financing the Out-of-Pocket Balance

blocks.text: After applying insurance benefits, many patients still have an out-of-pocket balance ranging from $500 to $4,000+ depending on case complexity and plan generosity. Our Markham clinic offers in-office payment plans with no interest for balances paid within 12 months, and referrals to dental financing providers offering extended terms of 24–60 months. Monthly payments on a $2,500 balance over 24 months are typically around $100 — manageable alongside other household expenses.

Patients who are self-employed or who have a health spending account (HSA) through their employer can use those funds to pay for Invisalign with pre-tax money. Dental expenses not reimbursed by insurance are also eligible for the federal Medical Expense Tax Credit, which can return meaningful dollars in tax savings for patients in higher income brackets.

sections.heading: Getting Your Insurance Picture Clarified Before You Start

blocks.text: The most empowering thing you can do before beginning Invisalign is to get a pre-determination from your insurer. Our clinic submits pre-determinations on behalf of every orthodontic patient — you will receive a written response from your insurer specifying exactly what they will pay toward your treatment before we make your first aligner. This eliminates billing surprises and allows you to plan your finances with accuracy.

[Book an Invisalign consultation](/appointments) at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham and bring your benefit card. We will run the benefit check, show you your ClinCheck smile simulation, and give you a complete financial picture — all at the same appointment. There is no obligation to proceed, and there is no guessing.

title: Retainers After Invisalign: How to Keep Your Results
seoTitle: Retainers After Invisalign: Keeping Your Results | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: Orthodontic results do not last without retainers. Learn the types of retainers available, how long to wear them, how to care for them and what happens if you stop.
excerpt: Teeth moved during Invisalign treatment will relapse — shift back toward their original positions — if retainers are not worn consistently after treatment. This guide explains the retention options, the wear schedule, and how to protect your investment for life.
intro: Finishing your last Invisalign aligner is an exciting milestone. But the end of active treatment is not the end of the process — it is the beginning of the retention phase, which is what keeps your teeth in their new positions permanently. Without consistent retainer wear, orthodontic relapse is essentially inevitable: the periodontal fibres that anchor teeth in bone have memory and will gradually pull teeth back toward their pre-treatment positions.

This article explains why retention is non-negotiable, the retainer options available at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) after Invisalign, how long and how often retainers need to be worn, and how to care for removable retainers over the years. If you have questions about retainers before your Invisalign treatment concludes, see our [Invisalign Markham guide](/blog/invisalign-markham-cost-timeline) for the full treatment picture.

sections.heading: Why Teeth Move After Orthodontic Treatment

blocks.text: During Invisalign treatment, aligner forces gradually move teeth through the bone. The bone remodels around the new tooth positions — dissolving on the pressure side and forming on the tension side. But this remodelling takes time to fully mature: for months after active treatment ends, the bone around the teeth is not yet fully mineralised, and the periodontal ligament fibres that attach the tooth to the bone retain their pre-treatment orientation and tension.

These immature fibres exert a pull on the teeth toward their old positions — a process called orthodontic relapse. The front teeth — particularly lower incisors — are the most susceptible to relapse because they are narrow, multiple, and subject to tongue pressure. Upper front teeth are typically more stable but still require retention. Without a retainer to counteract this pull, teeth will begin moving within weeks of completing Invisalign.

sections.heading: Types of Retainers

blocks.text: There are three main types of retainers, each with different characteristics. **Clear removable retainers** (like Vivera retainers made by Invisalign, or similar Essix-style retainers) look almost identical to Invisalign aligners. They are the most common choice after Invisalign because patients are already accustomed to clear tray wear. They are worn full-time for the first few months, then transitioned to nights-only wear. They need to be replaced every two to five years as the plastic ages.

items: **Clear removable retainer (Essix/Vivera):** most discreet, easy to wear, requires replacement every 2–5 years.
**Hawley retainer (wire and acrylic):** more durable, adjustable, allows teeth to settle into natural contact; more visible.
**Bonded/permanent retainer:** thin wire glued to the back of the lower (and sometimes upper) front teeth; maintenance-free, cannot be forgotten.
**Combination:** bonded wire for lower front teeth + clear retainer for upper arch is a popular approach at our clinic.
**Night guard retainer:** for patients who grind, a hard acrylic appliance that functions as both retainer and bruxism guard.

sections.heading: The Retention Wear Schedule

blocks.text: Dr. Kadivar prescribes a retention schedule based on your specific case. The standard protocol for clear removable retainers is: full-time wear (20–22 hours per day, removing only to eat and brush) for the first three to six months after active treatment ends. After this initial phase, nightly wear — every night without exception — is recommended indefinitely. The phrase often used is: wear your retainer as long as you want to keep your teeth straight.

Patients sometimes ask whether they can eventually stop wearing retainers at all. The honest answer is that after several years of consistent nighttime wear, many patients find they can reduce to four to five nights per week without perceptible relapse — but completely stopping, even after ten years, carries relapse risk. Teeth continue to experience natural forces throughout life, and some degree of retention is needed to counteract these forces indefinitely.

sections.heading: Caring for Removable Retainers

blocks.text: Clear retainer care is essentially identical to [Invisalign aligner care](/blog/how-to-care-for-invisalign-trays): rinse in cool water every time you remove them, brush gently with clear soap morning and evening, soak weekly in retainer cleaning solution, and store in the case provided when not in your mouth. The same rules apply — no hot water (warps the plastic), no toothpaste (scratches the surface), no coloured beverages while wearing.

Clear retainers develop micro-cracks and discolouration over time and will eventually need replacement. On average, a clear retainer lasts two to five years with proper care. Keep an eye on the fit: if the retainer no longer seats fully — if it feels like it is not quite covering the teeth completely — the retainer may have warped, or minor tooth movement may have occurred. Report either scenario to Dr. Kadivar promptly.

Replacement tip: Order a replacement retainer before your current one fails, not after. If your retainer breaks and you have no replacement, teeth can shift meaningfully within weeks. Many patients order a backup set of retainers at the completion of Invisalign and store them safely for exactly this situation.

sections.heading: Bonded Retainers: The Set-It-and-Forget-It Option

blocks.text: A bonded (permanent) retainer is a thin, flexible wire cemented to the back (lingual) surfaces of the front teeth — typically the lower four to six incisors, and sometimes the upper front teeth. Once placed, it cannot be removed by the patient and works continuously without any thought or compliance required. For patients who know they are unlikely to remember to wear a removable retainer consistently, a bonded retainer eliminates the relapse risk from forgotten wear.

Bonded retainers require some attention to hygiene: flossing requires a floss threader to pass the floss under the wire, and the wire must be cleaned thoroughly at every brushing. At professional cleaning appointments, the hygienist checks the wire for any detached bonding points — a partially debonded wire no longer holds the tooth and can actually push it out of position. Dr. Kadivar checks bonded retainers at every recall examination.

sections.heading: What Happens If You Stop Wearing Your Retainer?

blocks.text: The severity of relapse depends on how long retainers were worn before stopping, which teeth were moved, and individual biology. Lower front teeth are the first to show relapse, typically beginning within weeks of stopping retainer wear. The relapse is usually slowest in the first year and then accelerates as the periodontal fibres mature in their pre-treatment orientation.

If you have stopped wearing your retainer and notice your teeth shifting, contact Dr. Kadivar as soon as possible. Early relapse — within the first few months — may be addressed by a new retainer that applies gentle pressure to return teeth to their corrected positions. Significant relapse that has progressed over months or years may require a short course of refinement aligners to re-correct the movement, adding cost and time that consistent retainer wear would have prevented entirely.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Investment Long-Term

blocks.text: The Invisalign investment you made — financially and in terms of the months spent wearing aligners — is worth protecting. The cost of consistent retainer replacement over a lifetime is a small fraction of the cost of retreatment. Think of nighttime retainer wear as maintenance for your smile in the same way oil changes are maintenance for a car: routine, simple and vastly less expensive than the alternative.

At Smile Dental Arts Centre, we review your retainer fit at every regular dental examination so any issues are caught early. If you have lost or broken your retainer, [call us at (905) 604-7330](/contact-us) or [book online](/appointments) — we will arrange a replacement as quickly as possible to minimise any tooth movement during the gap.

title: Sedation Dentistry in Markham: Relax in the Chair
seoTitle: Sedation Dentistry Markham | Comfortable, Anxiety-Free Dental Care
metaDescription: Nervous about dental visits? Smile Dental Arts Centre offers nitrous oxide and oral sedation dentistry in Markham to help you relax. Book a comfortable appointment today.
excerpt: Sedation dentistry allows anxious patients to receive the dental care they need in complete comfort. Learn about your options at our Markham clinic.
intro: If the thought of sitting in a dental chair makes your palms sweat, you are not alone. Dental anxiety affects roughly one in six Canadians and causes many people to postpone—or skip entirely—the care their teeth need. Sedation dentistry in Markham changes that equation by using safe, carefully monitored medications to help you feel calm, comfortable, and in control throughout your appointment.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) we prioritise your comfort from the moment you walk through the door. Whether you need a routine cleaning or a longer restorative procedure, our team can tailor a sedation approach that lets you receive the full dental care you deserve—without fear getting in the way.

sections.heading: What Is Sedation Dentistry?

blocks.text: Sedation dentistry uses medication to reduce anxiety and increase comfort during dental procedures. Unlike general anaesthesia—which renders patients completely unconscious—dental sedation leaves you relaxed but still responsive. You can answer questions, follow simple instructions, and breathe on your own throughout the appointment.

items: **Nitrous oxide (laughing gas):** A colourless gas inhaled through a small nasal mask. It produces mild euphoria and relaxation within minutes and wears off almost immediately after the mask is removed.
**Oral sedation:** A prescription pill taken roughly an hour before your appointment. It produces moderate sedation; most patients feel drowsy and have little memory of the procedure.
**IV sedation:** Administered intravenously by a trained sedation provider. Rarely needed for routine care, but available for complex or lengthy procedures.

blocks.text: Nitrous oxide is the most common form of sedation at our Markham clinic. It is safe for most adults and children and has been used in dentistry for over 150 years.

sections.heading: Who Is a Good Candidate for Sedation?

blocks.text: Sedation dentistry is not just for people with extreme phobia. Many of our patients benefit from it for the following reasons:

items: Moderate to severe dental anxiety or a history of traumatic dental experiences
Sensitive gag reflex that makes treatment uncomfortable
Difficulty sitting still for longer appointments (e.g., full mouth restorations)
Complex treatment planned over multiple steps—sedation can allow more work to be completed in fewer visits
Patients with special health considerations who struggle with standard care

blocks.text: Our dentist will review your medical history and current medications at your [new patient consultation](/appointments) before recommending any sedation option.

sections.heading: Is Sedation Dentistry Safe?

blocks.text: When administered by a trained dental professional, sedation dentistry is very safe. The [Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario](https://www.rcdso.org/) sets strict standards for sedation in Ontario dental offices. Your vital signs are monitored throughout the procedure, and reversal agents are available if needed.

Nitrous oxide in particular has an excellent safety record. Because it is exhaled rapidly, you can typically drive yourself home after a nitrous-only appointment, although we always recommend having a companion if you feel uncertain.

blocks.title: Laughing gas at the dentist — what to expect from dental nitrous oxide (Teeth Talk Girl)

sections.heading: What to Expect at Your Sedation Appointment

items: **Before:** Share a complete list of medications and supplements. Arrange a driver if you are having oral sedation.
**Arrival:** Our team applies monitors and, for nitrous oxide, places the nasal mask before any treatment begins.
**During:** You remain conscious but deeply relaxed. Time may seem to pass quickly—a 90-minute appointment often feels like 20 minutes.
**After nitrous:** You feel normal within minutes and can return to daily activities. After oral sedation, rest at home for the remainder of the day.

blocks.text: Many patients who use sedation dentistry report that their appointment was so comfortable, they are no longer anxious about future visits—breaking the avoidance cycle that leads to bigger dental problems.

sections.heading: Book Your Comfortable Dental Appointment in Markham

blocks.text: You deserve dental care that feels manageable, not terrifying. If anxiety has kept you from the dentist, sedation may be the solution. Contact our [Markham dental office](/) or [book online](/appointments) to discuss which sedation option fits your needs.

We also offer [emergency dental care](/emergency-dentist-markham) for urgent situations and work with patients enrolled in the [Canadian Dental Care Plan](/canadian-dental-care-plan-cdcp) to keep care accessible.

title: Overcoming Dental Anxiety in Markham: A Gentle Approach
seoTitle: Dental Anxiety Markham | Gentle, Fear-Free Dentistry at Our Clinic
metaDescription: Dental anxiety shouldn't stop you from getting the care you need. Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham offers gentle, patient-centred care to help nervous patients feel at ease.
excerpt: Dental anxiety is extremely common, but it doesn't have to control your oral health. Discover how our Markham dental team creates a safe, judgement-free experience for anxious patients.
intro: Dental anxiety is one of the most common reasons Canadians delay or avoid dental care—and the consequences can be serious. Untreated cavities deepen, gum disease advances, and what started as a manageable problem can become an emergency. If fear of the dentist is holding you back, our Markham team has helped hundreds of anxious patients rebuild a positive relationship with dental care.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) we believe every patient deserves to feel safe, heard, and respected in the chair. We slow down, explain every step, and never make you feel embarrassed about your anxiety. Our goal is to work with you—not on you.

sections.heading: Why Dental Anxiety Happens

blocks.text: Dental anxiety can stem from a variety of sources, and understanding yours is the first step toward managing it:

items: **Past negative experiences:** Pain, unexpected procedures, or feeling out of control during a previous visit
**Fear of pain or needles:** Even if your last visit was pain-free, anticipatory anxiety can be just as powerful
**Embarrassment:** Worry about being judged for the state of your teeth after years away
**Sensory triggers:** The sounds, smells, and vibrations associated with dental equipment
**Feeling of helplessness:** Lying back with limited ability to speak or stop the procedure

blocks.text: You will never be judged at our clinic. No matter how long it has been since your last visit, we are here to help—not to lecture.

sections.heading: How We Make Dentistry More Comfortable

blocks.text: Our entire approach is designed to reduce anxiety at every touchpoint:

items: **Tell-show-do:** We explain what we're about to do, show you the instrument, then proceed—no surprises
**Stop signal:** You can raise your hand at any time and we will immediately pause
**Topical anaesthetic first:** We always apply a numbing gel before any injection so you don't feel the needle

title: Dental Bridge in Markham: Replace a Missing Tooth Without Surgery
seoTitle: Dental Bridge Markham | Fixed Tooth Replacement at Smile Dental Arts Centre
metaDescription: A dental bridge is a non-surgical way to replace one or more missing teeth. Learn about bridge types, costs, and care at our Markham dental clinic.
excerpt: A dental bridge uses crowns on neighbouring teeth to support a lifelike artificial tooth—filling a gap without surgery and restoring your ability to chew, speak, and smile with confidence.
intro: A missing tooth does far more damage than most people realise. Without the root stimulating the jawbone, bone begins to resorb. Surrounding teeth drift and tip into the gap, disrupting your bite. Over time, facial support is lost and premature ageing of the lower face occurs. A dental bridge in Markham addresses the gap quickly, without surgery, and protects the surrounding teeth and bone structure.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) we fabricate porcelain bridges that match your natural tooth colour precisely. Most bridges are completed in just two appointments, with a temporary bridge in place during the fabrication period so you are never without a full smile.

sections.heading: Types of Dental Bridges

blocks.text: Traditional (Fixed) Bridge

The most common type. Two dental crowns placed on the teeth on either side of the gap (abutment teeth) hold a false tooth (pontic) between them. Traditional bridges are highly durable and can last ten to fifteen years with proper care.
Cantilever Bridge
Used when there is only one adjacent tooth to anchor the pontic. Less common due to higher stress on the anchor tooth.
Implant-Supported Bridge
For patients replacing multiple adjacent teeth. [Dental implants](/dental-implants) act as anchors instead of crowns on natural teeth—protecting the remaining natural teeth from being reduced.

blocks.title: Porcelain crown and bridge procedure explained — step-by-step dental training video

sections.heading: The Bridge Procedure: What to Expect

items: **Appointment 1 — Preparation:** The abutment teeth are gently shaped to accommodate crowns. Impressions are taken and sent to the dental lab. A temporary bridge protects the prepared teeth.
**Between visits (2–3 weeks):** The lab crafts your permanent porcelain bridge to match the shade and shape of your natural teeth.
**Appointment 2 — Placement:** The temporary is removed, the permanent bridge is checked for fit and bite, then cemented into place.

blocks.text: Preparing abutment teeth is permanent—this is why [dental implants](/dental-implants) are often preferred when bone health allows, as implants don't require altering healthy neighbouring teeth.

sections.heading: Caring for Your Dental Bridge

items: Floss under the pontic daily using a floss threader or water flosser
Brush twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush
Avoid chewing ice, hard candies, or sticky foods directly on the bridge
Attend [regular professional cleanings](/teeth-cleaning-markham) every six months

sections.heading: Dental Bridge vs. Implant: Which Is Right for You?

blocks.text: Bridges provide a faster, less invasive solution for replacing a single missing tooth. Implants preserve more bone long-term and don't require altering adjacent teeth. The right choice depends on your bone density, budget, and how many teeth need replacing. Our team will walk you through both options during your consultation.

intro: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is the hinge that connects your jaw to your skull. sections.heading: Symptoms of TMJ Disorder

items: Jaw pain or soreness, especially in the morning
Clicking, popping, or grinding sounds when opening and closing the mouth
Difficulty or pain when chewing, yawning, or opening wide
Jaw locking in the open or closed position
Headaches, neck aches, or earaches with no other clear cause
Facial muscle tension or fatigue

blocks.text: TMJ symptoms often worsen with stress—which increases jaw clenching—and may fluctuate over weeks or months. Even if symptoms are mild, it's worth discussing them with your dentist.

sections.heading: What Causes TMJ Disorder?

items: [Bruxism (teeth grinding or clenching)](/bruxism-teeth-grinding-markham) — the most common dental cause of TMD
Bite misalignment that puts uneven pressure on the joint
Jaw injury or trauma
Arthritis in the temporomandibular joint
Stress and psychological tension held in the jaw muscles

sections.heading: TMJ Treatment Options

blocks.text: Occlusal Splint (Night Guard)

A custom-fitted oral appliance worn at night separates the teeth, relaxes the jaw muscles, and prevents clenching damage. See our detailed guide to [night guards](/night-guard-markham) for more information.
Bite Adjustment
If the bite is uneven due to high restorations or wear patterns, selective reshaping of the tooth surfaces can redistribute forces more evenly.
Physical Therapy and Jaw Exercises
Stretching and strengthening exercises for the jaw muscles can reduce tension and improve range of motion. Your dentist can provide a home exercise programme.
Medication
Short-term anti-inflammatories or muscle relaxants prescribed by your physician may help during acute flare-ups, complementing dental treatment.

sections.heading: When to See a Dentist About Jaw Pain

blocks.text: Any persistent jaw pain—especially if it's been present for more than two weeks—warrants a dental evaluation. sections.heading: What Causes Bruxism?

blocks.text: Bruxism is multifactorial—meaning several factors often contribute simultaneously:

Soft inner layer for comfort, hard outer layer for durability. A good middle-ground option.

Bring it to your check-up appointments so we can inspect it for wear

intro: Oral cancer is one of the most common cancers in Canada, affecting the lips, tongue, gums, cheeks, floor of the mouth, and throat. The good news: when detected early, five-year survival rates exceed 80%. When caught late, that figure drops to under 40%. A routine oral cancer screening at your Markham dental appointment takes less than five minutes—and it could save your life.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) our dentist performs a thorough oral cancer screening at every comprehensive exam. We look for lesions, abnormal tissue, asymmetries, and suspicious patches that warrant further investigation, referring promptly to a specialist when anything concerns us.

sections.heading: What Oral Cancer Screening Involves

blocks.text: The screening is simple and entirely pain-free:

items: **Visual inspection:** We examine the lips, gums, tongue, cheeks, floor of the mouth, palate, and the back of the throat under bright light.
**Manual palpation:** We feel the jaw, lymph nodes, and soft tissues of the neck for lumps, swelling, or asymmetry.
**Adjunctive technology:** Special blue light or fluorescence devices can help identify abnormal tissue that isn't yet visible to the naked eye.

blocks.title: How to do a mouth cancer check at home — from the Oral Health Foundation

sections.heading: Warning Signs to Watch Between Appointments

items: A sore, ulcer, or patch that does not heal within two weeks
Red or white patches on the gums, tongue, or lining of the mouth
Unexplained lumps or thickening of any oral tissue
Persistent sore throat, hoarseness, or difficulty swallowing
Numbness, pain, or tenderness anywhere in the mouth or face

blocks.text: If you notice any of these signs, do not wait for your next scheduled appointment. Contact our [Markham dental office](/) for an urgent assessment.

sections.heading: Who Is Most at Risk?

blocks.text: While anyone can develop oral cancer, certain factors increase risk:

items: Tobacco use (smoking or smokeless tobacco) — the single largest risk factor
Heavy alcohol consumption, especially combined with tobacco
HPV (human papillomavirus) infection — now the fastest-growing cause in younger patients
Prolonged sun exposure to the lips
Personal or family history of oral or other head and neck cancers
Age over 40 (though incidence is rising in younger adults)

blocks.text: The [Canadian Cancer Society](https://www.cancer.ca/) provides detailed resources on oral cancer risk reduction.

sections.heading: How Often Should You Be Screened?

blocks.text: Annual screening is recommended for all adults during a [regular dental check-up](/dental-checkup-markham). Higher-risk individuals (smokers, heavy drinkers) should be screened at every six-month visit. Our team includes oral cancer screening automatically in every comprehensive exam—no separate booking required.

metaDescription: Tooth sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweets can signal underlying problems. Smile Dental Arts Centre diagnoses the cause and provides lasting relief for sensitive teeth in Markham.
excerpt: Tooth sensitivity is a symptom, not a condition—meaning the right treatment depends on finding the cause. Our Markham dentists identify why your teeth hurt and provide lasting solutions.
intro: That sharp jolt of pain when you sip hot coffee or bite into ice cream is your tooth's way of telling you something is wrong. Tooth sensitivity is extremely common, but it is not normal—it is a signal that dentine (the inner layer of the tooth) has become exposed or that another underlying problem exists. Treating sensitivity effectively means identifying and addressing the root cause, not just masking the symptom.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) in Markham, we investigate the specific cause of your sensitivity at a [comprehensive examination](/new-patient-dental-exam-markham) before recommending any treatment. Whether the culprit is enamel erosion, gum recession, a cracked tooth, or early decay, we have targeted solutions that provide lasting relief.

sections.heading: Common Causes of Tooth Sensitivity

items: **Enamel erosion:** From acidic foods and drinks (citrus, soda, wine) or acid reflux — leaves dentine exposed
**Gum recession:** As gums pull back, sensitive root surfaces are exposed (see our [gum recession guide](/gum-recession-treatment-markham))
**Teeth grinding (bruxism):** Wears away enamel over time, creating widespread sensitivity
**Cracked tooth:** Even a hairline crack allows temperature and pressure to reach the nerve
**Tooth decay:** Cavities dissolve enamel, creating sensitivity before pain develops
**Over-whitening:** Excessive use of peroxide whitening products strips enamel temporarily

blocks.title: How gum recession causes tooth sensitivity — and what can be done about it

sections.heading: Treatment Options for Sensitive Teeth

blocks.text: In-Office Desensitising Treatments

Fluoride varnish or bonding agents applied directly to sensitive areas seal exposed dentinal tubules and provide immediate, lasting relief. This is the most effective single-visit treatment for mild to moderate sensitivity.
Dental Bonding or Crowns
For teeth with significant enamel loss or a cracked tooth, a composite bonding restoration or porcelain crown may be required to protect the tooth and eliminate sensitivity completely.
Night Guard for Bruxism
If grinding is the cause, a [custom night guard](/night-guard-markham) stops the enamel wear at the source.
Gum Grafting
When recession is significant, a connective tissue graft can restore gum coverage over exposed roots, both eliminating sensitivity and protecting against further bone and tissue loss.

Desensitising toothpastes (e.g., containing potassium nitrate or stannous fluoride) can provide modest relief, but they don't treat the underlying cause. Use them as a supplement, not a substitute, for professional care.

intro: Mints and mouthwash mask bad breath—they don't treat it. Persistent halitosis (the clinical term for chronic bad breath) is almost always caused by bacteria in the mouth producing sulfur compounds as they break down food and dead cells. items: **Gum disease (periodontitis):** Deep pockets of bacteria beneath the gumline produce a distinctively unpleasant sulfur odour
**Poor oral hygiene:** Plaque and food debris on teeth and the tongue feed bacteria
**Dental decay or failing restorations:** Cavities harbour bacteria and produce odour
**Dry mouth (xerostomia):** Saliva normally washes away bacteria; without it, they accumulate
**Tongue coating:** The back of the tongue is the most common single site for halitosis-causing bacteria
**Non-dental causes:** Sinus infections, tonsil stones, GERD, and certain foods (garlic, onion) can also contribute

blocks.text: Deep Cleaning (Scaling and Root Planing)

If gum disease is the culprit, a deep cleaning removes bacterial deposits from below the gumline — eliminating the primary odour source. Patients with periodontitis often notice a dramatic improvement in breath within days.
Cavity Treatment and Restoration Replacement
Decayed teeth and leaky old fillings harbour bacteria. Treating cavities and replacing failing restorations removes bacterial reservoirs that mouthwash cannot reach.
Professional Tongue Cleaning
At your [hygiene appointment](/teeth-cleaning-markham), our hygienist can perform professional tongue debridement and provide a tongue scraper with instructions for home use.

items: Brush twice daily, including your tongue, for a full two minutes

Use a tongue scraper every morning before brushing
Stay well hydrated to support salivary flow
Limit alcohol, coffee, and tobacco — all of which reduce saliva and increase odour

intro: Gum recession happens gradually—so gradually that many patients don't notice it until a dentist points it out, or until [tooth sensitivity](/sensitive-teeth-markham) becomes noticeable. As the gum tissue pulls away from the tooth, root surfaces become exposed. Roots lack the protective enamel coating of the crown, making them highly susceptible to decay and sensitivity. Over time, untreated recession can progress to tooth loss.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) in Markham, we offer a comprehensive evaluation of recession patterns to determine the cause and the best treatment strategy. Whether your recession is mild and manageable with improved home care, or significant enough to require a gum graft, we will guide you through every option with clear, honest advice.

sections.heading: What Causes Gum Recession?

items: **Aggressive brushing:** Scrubbing sideways with a hard-bristled brush is the most preventable cause
**Gum disease (periodontitis):** Bacterial infection destroys the tissue and bone that support the gum margin
**Genetic predisposition:** Thin gum tissue is inherited and more susceptible to recession
[**Bruxism (teeth grinding)**](/bruxism-teeth-grinding-markham): Excessive force on the teeth traumatises the surrounding tissue
**Misaligned bite or crowded teeth:** Creates areas of unequal pressure and inadequate tissue support
**Piercings:** Lip and tongue piercings repeatedly traumatise the gum margin

blocks.title: How to understand and address gum recession — Dr. Ellie Phillips explains causes and solutions

sections.heading: When Does Gum Recession Need to Be Treated?

blocks.text: Not all recession requires surgical intervention. Treatment decisions are based on:

items: How much root is exposed (measured in millimetres)
Whether the recession is stable or progressing
The thickness and width of remaining gum tissue
Whether roots are showing decay or sensitivity
The patient's long-term goals for the affected teeth

blocks.text: Mild recession with stable, thick gum tissue can often be managed with improved brushing technique and [regular professional cleanings](/teeth-cleaning-markham). A soft-bristled electric toothbrush makes a measurable difference.

sections.heading: Gum Grafting: Restoring Lost Tissue

blocks.text: When recession is significant, a connective tissue graft (the gold standard procedure) moves tissue from the palate or uses a donor tissue source to cover exposed roots. Benefits include:

items: Elimination or significant reduction of root sensitivity
Restored aesthetics — the 'long tooth' appearance is corrected
Root protection from decay
Prevention of further recession and bone loss

blocks.text: Recovery after grafting takes approximately two weeks. The grafted tissue establishes its own blood supply and integrates with the surrounding tissue over the following months.

sections.heading: Denture Reline: When the Base Still Works

blocks.text: A reline adds new material to the fitting surface of the denture, restoring its fit to the changed contour of the jawbone. This is usually possible when the teeth themselves are in good condition and only the fit has changed.
Chairside Reline
A faster process performed in the office using temporary material. Good for urgent situations, but typically lasts 1–2 years.
Laboratory Reline
Your denture is sent to a dental lab overnight or for a few days. Results in a more precise fit using permanent material.

sections.heading: When Is It Time for New Dentures?

blocks.text: Dentures generally last 5–10 years before replacement is recommended. Signs it's time for new dentures include:

items: The denture no longer stays in place even after relining
The bite has changed significantly — you notice your chin moving closer to your nose
Teeth are severely worn and chewing efficiency has declined
The acrylic base is cracked in multiple places or has been repaired multiple times

blocks.text: Consider discussing [implant-supported dentures](/dental-implants) — they eliminate movement, dramatically improve chewing, and slow ongoing bone loss.

metaDescription: Wondering what tooth extraction costs in Markham? Learn about simple and surgical extraction pricing, insurance coverage, and what the procedure involves at our clinic.
excerpt: Tooth extraction costs in Markham vary based on the tooth's position and complexity. Here's a transparent breakdown of what to expect—and how insurance and the CDCP may help cover the cost.
intro: Cost is often the first question patients ask when they learn a tooth needs to come out—and it's a fair one. Tooth extraction fees in Markham range from straightforward to more complex depending on whether the tooth is fully erupted and accessible (simple extraction) or impacted, curved, or broken at the gumline (surgical extraction). Knowing what to expect in advance helps you plan and avoid surprises.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) we provide written cost estimates before every extraction and bill your insurance directly. Our priority is always to save a tooth when possible—but when extraction is the right decision, we ensure it is performed as comfortably and efficiently as possible.

sections.heading: Simple vs. Surgical Extraction: What's the Difference?

blocks.text: Simple Extraction

A tooth that is fully erupted above the gumline and has a single or straightforward root can be removed with forceps under local anaesthetic. Most routine extractions of back molars or damaged front teeth fall into this category. Cost range: approximately $150–$300.
Surgical Extraction

When a tooth is impacted (wisdom teeth), broken below the gumline, or has curved/fused roots, a surgical approach is needed. This involves making a small incision in the gum and sometimes removing a small amount of bone. Cost range: approximately $250–$600 per tooth.

blocks.title: What really happens during wisdom teeth removal — dentist reveals the procedure (The Bentist)

sections.heading: Does Insurance Cover Tooth Extraction?

blocks.text: Most dental insurance plans in Canada cover tooth extractions as a basic restorative benefit, typically at 70–80% of the fee guide rate after the deductible. Some plans cover surgical extractions at 50–80%. Your annual maximum and remaining benefits determine what you will owe.
The [Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)](/canadian-dental-care-plan-cdcp) also covers extractions for eligible patients. We verify your CDCP eligibility and coverage at your appointment.
If you need multiple extractions, we can sequence them across two insurance calendar years to maximise your benefit coverage and reduce out-of-pocket costs.

sections.heading: After Extraction: Next Steps

blocks.text: After a tooth is removed, it's important to plan for replacement. Leaving a gap leads to bone resorption, teeth shifting, and bite problems over time. Options include:

items: [Dental implant](/dental-implants) — the most natural long-term replacement, preserving bone
[Dental bridge](/dental-bridge-markham) — a fixed option that spans the gap using adjacent teeth
Partial denture — a removable option; more affordable but less stable

blocks.text: Our team will discuss your replacement options at the same appointment so you can make an informed decision from the start.

sections.heading: Post-Extraction Care

items: Bite firmly on gauze for 30–45 minutes after the procedure to control bleeding
Do not smoke, use straws, or rinse forcefully for 24 hours — this protects the blood clot
Eat soft foods on the opposite side for 2–3 days
Take any prescribed pain medication as directed
Return if you experience increasing pain after day 3 — this may indicate dry socket, which we treat quickly

intro: No matter how diligent your home oral hygiene routine, there are places your toothbrush and floss simply cannot reach effectively. Plaque hardens into tartar (calculus) within 24–72 hours, and once mineralised, it can only be removed with professional instruments. Professional teeth cleaning—performed by a registered dental hygienist—removes this buildup, polishes tooth surfaces, and gives your dentist the opportunity to assess for early problems.

At [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/) in Markham, our hygiene appointments are thorough, comfortable, and educational. We don't just clean your teeth—we show you where your home routine needs improvement and how to address it, so you leave with healthier gums and a plan to keep them that way.

sections.heading: What a Professional Teeth Cleaning Includes

items: **Scaling:** Removal of plaque and tartar from all tooth surfaces, including below the gumline, using hand instruments and/or ultrasonic scalers
**Root planing (if needed):** Smoothing root surfaces to remove embedded bacteria and encourage gum reattachment in cases of early gum disease
**Polishing:** A gritty polish removes surface stains and leaves teeth smooth, making it harder for plaque to reattach
**Fluoride treatment:** A strengthening fluoride varnish or gel applied at the end of the appointment to remineralise early weak spots in enamel
**Oral hygiene review:** Personalised flossing and brushing technique coaching based on what we observe in your mouth

blocks.title: Professional teeth cleaning and whitening tips from a dental hygienist

sections.heading: How Often Do You Need a Professional Cleaning?

blocks.text: Most adults benefit from a professional cleaning every six months. Patients with gum disease, a high cavity rate, or systemic conditions that affect oral health (such as diabetes) are often recommended for three- to four-month hygiene intervals.
Children should receive their first cleaning around age one, or when their first tooth erupts — whichever comes first, according to the [Canadian Dental Association](https://www.cda-adc.ca/).
Skipping professional cleanings doesn't just allow tartar to build up — it allows gum disease to advance silently. Periodontal disease is the leading cause of adult tooth loss in Canada.

sections.heading: Deep Cleaning vs. Regular Cleaning

blocks.text: A regular preventive cleaning (prophylaxis) addresses plaque and tartar at and slightly below the gumline in healthy or mildly inflamed gums. A deep cleaning (scaling and root planing) goes significantly deeper, removing bacteria from infected pockets and smoothing root surfaces — it is a treatment for existing gum disease, not a prevention appointment.
If it's been more than 12–18 months since your last cleaning, expect that more time and potentially more appointments may be needed to fully address the accumulated buildup.
